Checking Your Own Credit Never Lowers Your Score – Applying for Credit Can

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (462 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Moneycrashers

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Check your own credit report and score as often as you like, since your own checks are soft inquiries that never affect your score.
  • Sources indicate that an inquiry is hard when a lender checks your credit because you applied to borrow from it.
  • In a recent development, according to FICO, a utility checking your credit to set a security deposit makes a soft inquiry.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Check your own credit report and score as often as you like, since your own checks are soft inquiries that never affect your score. A hard inquiry, the check a lender makes when you apply for credit, can take a few points off your FICO scores for a year, so space your applications several months apart.

Sources indicate that an inquiry is hard when a lender checks your credit because you applied to borrow from it. Nearly everything else is soft. The Consumer Financial Protection Bureau lists your own requests for your reports, the checks behind pre-approved offers, your current lenders’ account reviews, and employment screening among soft inquiries. Those never affect your credit scores, and neither does checking whether a card issuer will pre-approve you before you apply.

In a recent development, according to FICO, a utility checking your credit to set a security deposit makes a soft inquiry. Most checks by phone carriers and landlords don’t affect your FICO scores either, though some can, depending on how the credit bureau has classified the carrier or landlord. And asking for a higher credit limit can mean a hard inquiry at some card issuers and a soft one at others.

In a recent development, even a hard inquiry costs little. FICO claims one more takes less than five points off most people’s scores, and it counts for a year, though it stays on your report for up to two. Several at once weigh more than a single one, since a burst of applications makes it look as if you’re taking on more debt, and each hits harder when your credit history is short or holds few accounts. Rate shopping is the exception, because FICO treats several applications for one mortgage, car loan, or student loan as a single inquiry within a short window.

Picture someone who checks her score every week in her card’s app and never loses a point. Then she applies for three store cards in one month, and her score dips, because each application added a hard inquiry.

So check your own credit as often as you like, starting with your reports from all three credit bureaus, free every week at AnnualCreditReport.com. Apply only for credit you need, and leave several months between applications.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Find the conditions that waive your monthly checking fee and meet the easiest one, which may only mean sending part of your paycheck to the account. If none fits, ask the bank to move you to its basic account, or switch to a free checking account elsewhere.

A $15 monthly maintenance fee on checking costs $180 a year, for the kind of account many banks offer free.

In a recent development, your account’s page on the bank’s website and its fee schedule list the ways to avoid the fee, and you may be close to meeting one already. Chase Total Checking, for example, charges $15 a month but nothing for a statement period with $500 in qualifying electronic deposits, such as a paycheck or government benefits.

Sources indicate that A balance of at least $1,500 at the start of every day also waives the fee, and so does a $5,000 daily average, counting linked Chase savings and investments. The $1,500 balance is the easiest of the three to miss, since one day that starts below $1,500 rules that option out for the whole period.

Say your paycheck goes to a credit union and your Chase account charges $15 a month. If your employer lets you split your direct deposit, send a fixed $500 of each paycheck to Chase and the rest to the credit union, and you save $180 a year. A Zelle transfer, cash, or a check won’t count toward the $500.

According to recent reports, if no condition fits, call the bank and ask to move to its basic account. Chase Secure Banking, for one, charges $4.95 a month but nothing for a statement period with $250 in qualifying electronic deposits, though it has no paper checks or outgoing wire transfers. On the same call, ask for the last few months’ fees back, along with any other fee you find by adding up a year of bank fees.

If you’d still pay a fee, open a free checking account at an online bank or credit union.

To pick one, compare the best free checking accounts.

  • As our financial world has been whipped around like a circus tent in a hurricane for the last several months, almost everyone who has a stake in this country has been wondering what to make of it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Quite accidentally, it looks like we timed our last talk about the stock market pretty darned well. Back in February 2025, the market put the perfect cap on a multi year climb before stepping onto the wild roller coaster we’re presently riding. Since then it has seen some of the steepest drops and recoveries in history, losing a full 20% of its value at the bottom while somehow managing to end up right back near the peak as I’m writing this.

And although stock market volatility doesn’t always come with an easily labeled explanation, this time the reason seems pretty clear: it’s the Tariffs.

As our financial world has been whipped around like a circus tent in a hurricane for the last several months, almost everyone who has a stake in this country has been wondering what to make of it.

Industry observers note that as I write this, we still don’t know the outcome of the worldwide tariff and trade battle that our unpredictable government has unleashed upon the world. But we’re already seeing the results: businesses are bracing for massive changes, currencies and interest rates are reacting, and regular investors like you and me are wondering what the future holds for our early retirement funds. Surveying my own group of friends, the reactions span the whole range of emotions from “this is a giant Nothingburger” to “we’re all totally screwed.”.

Industry observers note that so what’s the real answer? To get closer to that, we should start with the most basic question of:.

In a recent development, A tariff is just a sales tax charged by our government on goods which are imported into the country. They are paid by whoever is doing the importing – meaning you if you order something like an e-bike directly from a company in China, or by companies like Amazon, Walmart, or Apple which import products from other countries by the shipload.

According to recent reports, but in the end, the tariffs aren’t paid by China or Amazon or Apple. They are paid by you, the end consumer, because if their cost of goods increases, a retailer is of course going to raise their prices to continue to make a profit.

Tariffs also affect companies directly: if Home Depot wants to build a upcoming store or Chevron needs a new oil rig, the tariffs on imported steel, copper, lumber and a million other components will raise the cost of these construction projects. And they raise the cost of housing, because most of the building materials in houses come from multiple countries as well.

On average, tariffs will result in higher prices for everything just like any other broad-based sales tax. And just like most other taxes, the overall effect is to slow the economy and reduce our spending power. On the positive side, all that tax money flows into the government’s pocket which could help fund the national budget and even reduce the deficit.

Of course, every government needs at least some tax revenue to function, so it makes sense to use some mix of sales, income and corporate taxes to get there. The most vital part is that the levels need to be as low as possible while still keeping the country running well, and as fair and predictable as possible, so that people and businesses have an incentive to work hard and the ability to initiative far into the future.

Recent findings suggest that and that’s where our current tariff regime gets it completely backwards. Donald Trump is throwing around random, extremely high tariff numbers as threats, then walking them back and changing them on an almost daily basis..

Whoa, that Sounds Mostly Bad – Is There a Good Side of Tariffs?

Sometimes, a country will use tariffs to protect their own domestic industries. For example, if you put a tax on imported Hondas, then General Motors cars will gain a competitive advantage – so GM will make more money. In this example, most consumers end up losing due to increased prices and decreased selection. But at least domestic auto manufacturers and their employees are happy.

This can be strategic (for example we might want to slap a tax on imported fighter jets to make sure Boeing and Lockheed can remain in business, for national defense purposes.) Or it can be corrupt (a politician might receive funding from kingpins in the steel industry, and in return then push through tariffs on imported steel to protect the profits of US steelmakers.).

And this isn’t just a Trump or Republican thing either – Joe Biden used tariffs during his terms in an attempt to please swing-state voters. One of the worst examples was a tax on imported solar panel components (which Trump has since raised even further, proving that Boneheadedness can be Bipartisan). These are sheets of cheap glass that literally pump the cheapest energy and easiest wealth into your country for 30 years as soon as you plug them in. Cheap energy lowers everyone’s cost of living while also boosting industry. There is no good reason to block such wealth from flowing across your borders.

Can Tariffs Bring Us More Jobs?

Let’s go back to that hypothetical tax on Hondas, and let’s say it’s a big one like $5000. At that level, many buyers will start heading over to the GM dealer next door to consider what he’s selling. Sure, the GM cars may not be as good, but for five grand some people are going to settle in order to save some money.

In a recent development, because of this, GM’s sales go up. So they hire more employees and build more factories. They might even develop some latest models and new technologies in response to all that new demand. More people learn advanced skills and in the best case it becomes a virtuous circle.

In a recent development, but in exchange for this boom in the auto industry, everyone else has to pay more for slightly shittier cars and trucks. Higher vehicle prices means Amazon will have to spend more on their delivery fleet, so they will raise prices slightly on everything they sell. Somewhere a startup firm or a medical breakthrough will be just a bit less likely to happen, because they are operating in an environment that is just a bit more expensive and a bit less efficient.

On top of that, with GM liberated from the hassle of competing with Honda, it will have less incentive to innovate and streamline itself. So its overall trajectory will be slower and less efficient even if its profits are higher.

It has been revealed that this big picture effect is why most economists agree that tariffs should be used very sparingly. They almost always cause unexpected damage, decrease overall employment and slow down an economy, but sometimes (like for food security or national defense) those costs are worth paying.

So Why is Donald Trump Throwing Around Tariffs Like They Are The Best Thing Ever?

This has been confusing to almost everyone. If you take him at his word, he appears to have a Bizarro Opposite Universe belief system about economics. Donald has claimed in speeches that the tariffs will somehow make us wealthier. He’s focusing on the first-order effects like GM hiring more workers, while completely ignoring the fact that everything else in the country gets less efficient in exchange.

But when he announces larger tariffs, share prices go down, because everyone who actually runs or invests in US companies knows that of course they will make less money on average. When tariffs are paused or reduced, share prices go back up. Yet he keeps wielding the threats and we go back and forth.

It seems to be obvious to everyone except Donald himself that Tariffs are just a national sales tax rather than some clever sneaky strategic weapon, which leads to various theories that okay, maybe he knows that too but is just pretending in order to gain some influence.

The basic theory goes like this:.

So right now our entire economy is subject to the whims of a single person.. And as long as this is the case, we’re just the same as any other dictatorship – something our constitution was supposed to prevent with the whole “three independent branches of government” thing.

But presidents have tried to break out of their constitutional cage and get more power many times in the past, and this is just the latest example. The real test will be if our system eventually manages to stop this abuse and put itself back in balance as it always has in the past. You can already see this fight beginning to play out in our court system, in this Economist article:.

How Big are the Tariffs Right Now?

Recent findings suggest that even without the 145% nonsense numbers that were thrown around a few months ago, they are still far higher than they have been in the last 75 years or more. While it would be hard to pin down the current numbers in a stationary blog post like this one, the key thing to remember is that our current US economy is built around very low tariffs and relatively free trade.

Why haven’t I noticed Prices Going Up Yet?

While the US economy is fueled by a constant stream of cargo ships, as a whole we function like the biggest cargo ship of all: we have a huge inventory and it takes a while to change directions.

So in normal times, we already have several months of inventory of most things in the country. And then when all this drama started, importers started placing even more orders to stockpile things in advance before the tariffs hit. And now that they are in place, we’re importing a lot less stuff.

Recent findings suggest that for now, we’re still using up the stockpiled inventory, but imports have dropped significantly so we’re rapidly running out of cheap goods. If that happens, we will probably start seeing shortages and price increases throughout this summer or fall. For some things like plastic party trinkets, we can do just fine without. But if we lose access to core useful things like tools and machinery, the economic consequences will be much less fun.

The Dark Side and the Bright Side.

The most important phrase to remember in US politics and economics is the phrase “This too shall pass.” The only mystery right now is that we don’t know exactly how it will pass. So we could sketch out a few scenarios:.

1) The current crazy-high tariffs really do stick around:.

In a recent development, I personally think this is the less likely scenario because nobody really wants it. But just as a thought experiment, it might go something like this:.

2) They do end up being just a negotiating tactic and we go back to mostly low tariffs.

In other words, the best way to win the tariff game is not to play it.

In a recent development, just as much of US prosperity is built upon our huge population of 330 million people living in 50 states with open borders and no trade restrictions, all (friendly) countries of the world can benefit from the free exchange of goods, services and even people. We’re all human beings and if we treat each other with a collaborative respect, we all grow richer.

Epilogue: Is it Almost Over Already?

I started writing this article on April 2nd, when Donald announced his “Liberation Day” and the stock market reacted with the biggest drop since 1932. Some people panicked and locked in significant losses despite decades of warnings from your favorite financial bloggers, like this unfortunate soul in the comments to a JL Collins post:.

But as I watched over the next two months, we have bounced our way back up – with each drop in proposed tariffs triggering a corresponding increase in stock prices (a measure of investor enthusiasm of how bright our future looks).

Industry observers note that right now, the US stock market is just about back to its all-time high. This doesn’t match with our current level of tariffs, which are still about seven times higher than they were before the circus opened. But it shows that investors believe it’s all going to end with a truce and a resumption of free-ish international trade.

If they’re wrong, the roller coaster ride will still have some more fun in store for us. But as long as we eventually end our current experiment in “emergency” tariff dictatorship and get back to functioning as a democracy, things should be just fine in the long run. I’m still 100% invested myself, so that’s where I place my bet.

The Biggest Lesson: Don’t Form Your Opinions Based on News Headlines.

It has been revealed that decades ago in a brighter age of journalism, there may have been a time when headlines were designed primarily to inform us, with just a bit of sizzle and spice to pull in our attention. Unfortunately, nowadays the priorities have flipped where the primary goal is attention, and accuracy carries little or no weight. Even a totally inaccurate article makes money for the publisher.

So while Democrats and Republicans like to do battle over which media sources are biased, in reality they’re all wrong: all click-funded commercial media is biased – sometimes politically but even more importantly biased towards generating outrage and fear, because those generate more money.

There are two solutions to this:.

1) Either ignore the media completely and focus on your own life, or.

2) Become a subject matter expert on things you really care about, and then read the original sources whenever you want to learn about something.

Sources indicate that I mostly practice option #1, but as a science and technology nerd I get into #2 in just the areas I find most interesting. And it’s amazing how the more deeply you understand a subject, the more you see just how wrong most media stories are about your area of expertise. Which means they’re probably pretty wrong about almost everything.

So as always, with this lesson learned it’s time to shut down that phone and laptop, exhale all our worries and get back outside with your real-life family and friends. See you in a few months!

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A REIT, or real estate investment trust, owns income property and must pay out most of its taxable income as dividends. To add real estate without becoming a landlord, buy a low-cost REIT index fund and hold it in an IRA or 401(k), where you owe no tax on those dividends each year.

If you own a total stock market index fund, you already own some REITs, but only a sliver. Real estate makes up 2.1% of Vanguard’s total stock market ETF.

Sources indicate that A REIT index fund raises your real estate share in one purchase. Its holdings are mostly equity REITs, which collect rent on property from apartments and warehouses to cell towers and data centers. Schwab U.S. REIT ETF holds about 120 of them and charges 0.07% of your investment a year. It leaves out mortgage REITs, which lend to property owners instead of owning buildings. Vanguard Real Estate ETF charges 0.13% a year. Both trade on a stock exchange, so you can sell shares on any day the market is open.

The other two ways to own REITs take more work or cost more than an index fund. Picking individual REITs means judging each organization’s cash flow and debt yourself. Non-traded REITs don’t trade on an exchange and are hard to sell, whether you buy them from a broker or a real estate crowdfunding app. The SEC states sales commissions and upfront fees on the ones brokers and advisers sell usually total about 9% to 10% of your investment.

Put 5% to 10% of your portfolio in the fund. A REIT has to pay out at least 90% of its taxable income as dividends, and you pay the income tax on them. Nareit, the REIT industry’s trade association, found 79% of the REIT dividends it tracked for 2025 were ordinary income. That part is taxed at your regular rate, not the lower rate other companies’ dividends can get.

Most of that income qualifies for a 20% deduction, a break the 2025 tax law made permanent, but in a taxable account you still owe tax on the dividends every year.

So buy the fund in an IRA, where its dividends aren’t taxed as they’re paid, or in your 401(k) if its menu includes a REIT index fund.

According to recent reports, picture this: you're settling into a lie-flat business class seat somewhere over the Atlantic, a glass of something cold in hand, knowing that in 48 hours you'll be waking up in Istanbul — and then, a few days later, continuing onward to Bangkok. Two bucket-list cities. One award booking. One points balance. This is what the Aeroplan stopover sweet spot feels like in practice. It's not a trick or a loophole — it's a deliberately designed feature of Air Canada's Aeroplan program that the vast majority of travelers simply don't know exists. And that gap between awareness and reality is exactly where the ChooseFI community finds its edge. Here's the math that should make your jaw drop. A business class itinerary from North America to Istanbul with a continuing flight onward to Bangkok — two long-haul segments, lie-flat seats, Star Alliance lounges at every connection — would cost somewhere between **$6,000 and $15,000 in cash**. That's a realistic retail range depending on season and how far out you book. Most people never consider it a possibility for a family vacation or a milestone trip because the sticker price puts it in a different universe. With Aeroplan, you're booking that same itinerary — the same seats, the same lounges, the same Turkish Airlines or Thai Airways product — for **75,000 Aeroplan points**. At the low end of the cash price range, that's already **8 cents per point**. At the high end, you're extracting **20 cents per point** from a currency that most people earned by putting groceries on a credit card. The pricing inefficiency here is structural. Aeroplan's partner award chart prices long-haul business class at a fixed rate regardless of cash fare fluctuations. When business class prices spike — around holidays, during peak travel seasons, during major events — your points cost stays exactly the same. You're insulated from the market. That's the FI mindset applied to travel: you've already paid for the trip in points, slowly accumulated through everyday spending, and now you're simply redeeming the stored value. The stopover itself is nearly free. Aeroplan charges just 5,000 extra miles to add a stopover city to a one-way award. That means your Istanbul layover becomes a multi-day stay — at zero additional points cost beyond that small add-on — and you haven't booked a second award at all. One booking. Two destinations. That's the entire premise, and once you see it, you can't unsee it.

The mechanism behind this sweet spot is elegantly simple once you understand it, but it requires knowing three things that most travelers don't: how Aeroplan's routing rules work, what a stopover actually is in the context of an award ticket, and why Star Alliance's global network makes this scalable to almost any destination pair you can imagine.

When Aeroplan relaunched its loyalty program in 2020, it did something remarkable: it eliminated fuel surcharges entirely and published a partner award chart with fixed pricing for flights on Star Alliance carriers. This is critical. When you book Turkish Airlines business class through Aeroplan, you pay the Aeroplan fixed chart rate — not what Turkish Airlines would charge in its own currency or miles program, and not the inflated cash price. That fixed chart is the engine of this redemption.

According to recent reports, for long-haul international business class, Aeroplan's chart prices routing through multiple regions based on your origin and destination — not every intermediate stop. This is the aha moment. Aeroplan determines your award price based on where your journey starts and where it ends, and then allows you to add a stopover in between for just 5,000 additional miles. The stopover city is priced as a pass-through for the purpose of calculating your award zone, not as a second trip.

On a one-way Aeroplan award, you're permitted to add a free stopover — meaning you can stay in an intermediate city for any length of time before continuing to your final destination. That 5,000-mile add-on is essentially the cost of a full additional destination. Compare that to booking a second one-way award from Istanbul to Bangkok, which would cost you another 40,000–55,000 Aeroplan points in business class. The math is decisive.

The routing must be geographically sensible — you can't fly backwards across the globe — but Aeroplan's allowance for multi-segment itineraries through Star Alliance hubs gives you enormous flexibility. Istanbul (IST) is a Turkish Airlines hub. Bangkok (BKK) is served by Thai Airways and several Star Alliance carriers. Both are Star Alliance partners. Both are bookable through Aeroplan at fixed chart rates with no fuel surcharges.

It has been revealed that booking an Aeroplan stopover award in business class is genuinely one of the more complex redemptions in the travel rewards world, but it becomes manageable when you break it into distinct phases. Here's exactly how to do it.

Start by deciding on your two destinations. Aeroplan stopovers work best when your intermediate city is a major Star Alliance hub that lies geographically between your origin and final destination. Classic combinations include North America to Istanbul (Turkish Airlines hub) continuing to Southeast Asia, or North America to a European hub continuing to the Middle East or East Africa. Your stopover city should be somewhere you genuinely want to spend 2–5 days — this is a real trip, not just a layover.

This is the most key and most time-consuming step. You need to find saver-level business class availability on both segments independently before you book.

Once you've confirmed availability on both segments, go to aeroplan.com and use the multi-city search function. Enter your full itinerary — origin, stopover city with your intended layover dates, and final destination.

In a recent development, A stopover is an intentional break in your journey lasting more than 24 hours at a connecting city. Most airlines treat stopovers as separate tickets, charging full price for each segment. Aeroplan is one of the few programs that allows a free stopover on round-trip awards, letting you explore a connecting city for days before continuing to your final destination. This is fundamentally different from a layover, which is a brief connection of a few hours at an airport. The stopover must be in a city served by a Star Alliance carrier on your routing, and the key is that Aeroplan prices the entire itinerary as one award, not two.

Call Aeroplan or use the multi-city search tool online. Specify your stopover city and duration (up to the maximum allowed). The system prices it as one round-trip award. Confirm total points match expectations before completing the booking.

No, stopovers are only available on round-trip awards through Aeroplan. One-way bookings do not qualify for the free stopover benefit. This is one reason round-trip awards can offer better value than two one-ways.

In a recent development, aeroplan has improved its online multi-city search tool, and some stopover itineraries can now be booked online. However, complex routings may still require a phone call. When calling, clearly state you want a round-trip award with a stopover and specify your stopover city and dates.

The best stopover cities are Star Alliance hub cities with strong business class availability: Istanbul (Turkish Airlines hub), Zurich (SWISS hub), Vienna (Austrian hub), Singapore (Singapore Airlines hub), and Tokyo (ANA hub). These hubs offer the most consistent saver-level award space.

It has been revealed that this sweet spot was last verified over 90 days ago. Award availability and pricing may have changed — verify current rates before booking.

Recent findings suggest that the Aeroplan stopover is one of the most powerful tools in the travel rewards playbook. By adding a free stopover to a round-trip business class award, you can explore two world-class cities for the points cost of visiting one. It requires planning, patience at the 355-day booking window, and comfort with Star Alliance routing rules, but the payoff is extraordinary: 10-15 cents per point in value on experiences that would cost thousands in cash. For the FI community member who has mastered basic award bookings and is ready to level up, this is the redemption that changes how you think about travel.

Industry observers note that are you trying to win the Mega Millions, but your numbers never seem to come up? It may be time to look for better ways to make money. Fortunately, you can earn extra cash without going and getting a “real job.”.

Sources indicate that what are the best ways to avoid sitting in a cubicle all day? Some money-making strategies require an upfront investment, while others let you earn money in your free time with the help of apps.

Read on to learn the best ways to earn cash without a regular 9-5 job, plus tips on how almost anyone can get started.

It has been revealed that one of the easiest ways to earn money is by signing up to participate in market research studies. You won’t make much, a few dollars here and there, but you can create a free account and get started within minutes.

You’ll be paid in PayPal cash or gift cards for sharing your opinion and completing other tasks online.

According to recent reports, E-Poll Market Research is one of the top companies to consider for this type of work. They make it easy to create an account and answer survey questions.

However, there are plenty of other options to consider, including:.

While market research gigs won’t make you rich, it’s something you can do during your spare time.

Industry observers note that if you have a book idea, turning your story into an eBook can help you earn passive income without a regular job. Kindle Direct Publishing can even help you format your book for Kindle, at which point you can market and sell your book to millions of potential readers who shop on Amazon.com.

It has been revealed that how much can you earn writing eBooks? That depends on how many books you write, how much you sell them for, and how successful you are at marketing your book. Selling 20 books per month with a profit of $7 per book would net you $140 per month and $1,680 per year.

Industry observers note that meanwhile, selling 100 books per month at $7 per book would net you $700 per month and $8,400 per year. Need a little inspiration? Here’s an article that shows you how to make your first $1,000 selling eBooks.

You can earn a lot of money by starting a blog or niche website and monetizing it. I should know. I started Good Financial Cents more than a decade ago, and have earned millions of dollars through the monetization of this site since its earliest days.

Sources indicate that how do you make money blogging? Earning real income with a website isn’t as easy as it looks, but there are plenty of monetization strategies you can try.

Here are the most common ways blogs make money:.

If you’re curious about what it takes to earn money blogging, consider signing up for my Make 1K Challenge. It’s free and can help you earn your first $1,000 online with some of the blog monetization strategies I’ve already mentioned.

You could argue that freelance work is like a regular job, but working at home and on your terms is much different from traditional employment. The fact is, most freelancers are fully remote – they can work from anywhere in the world with a laptop and an internet connection.

Plus, they can hire and fire clients based on their personal needs and preferences, and their income potential is unlimited. According to ZipRecruiter, freelancers in the U.S. average $63.53 per hour.

Of course, you’ll need a marketable skill to find paid work as a freelancer. This could be freelance writing, design skills, marketing expertise, or something else.

You can use several websites to market your skills as a freelancer, including:.

HealthyWage makes it possible to earn money while you lose weight. You won’t earn a ton of cash through the app, but you can earn a few dollars and use it to supplement other income you have.

The more weight you lose, the more money you can make. For example, the HealthyWage website claims some of their clients who lost more than 100 pounds managed to earn anywhere from $1,400 to $3,000.

However, the HW weight loss calculator shows potential earnings of $578 to $828 for people who only have 15 pounds to lose.

Recent findings suggest that if you have a car you rarely use and want to earn some side income, you can consider renting it out with Turo, a ride-sharing platform that connects car owners with people who need a short-term rental. You can set your price, although you’ll have more success if you price your car competitively.

Sources indicate that nicer vehicles in high-demand areas can easily fetch rates that surpass $100 per day through this platform. Turo notes that in-demand cars rented out regularly can bring in anywhere from $10,000 to $20,000 per year in net profit.

Industry observers note that plus, almost anyone can rent out their car provided it meets the guidelines of the Turo platform. Your car must be 12 years old or newer with less than 130,000 miles. It must be worth less than $200,000 (no Lambo’s), and you must also meet Turo’s auto insurance requirements.

In a recent development, do you have a spare bedroom in your home that you never use? Maybe you have a basement or garage apartment you could fix up and begin renting for a profit?

Recent findings suggest that either way, Airbnb lets you rent out rooms and other spaces in your home on any dates you prefer. You must let renters know they’re renting a room in a home vs. an entire apartment or house and provide as much additional detail as possible.

The amount you can earn will depend on where you live and the type of accommodation you can offer. However, expensive cities like Chicago, Latest York, and San Francisco have plenty of rooms for rent that go for well over $100 per night.

You may not have an entire room you can rent, but even if you have some storage space, Neighbor.com allows you to rent it out to others in need.

Common spaces rented through this platform include.

Recent findings suggest that the Neighbor.com platform makes it easy to advertise your unused space so that people nearby can inquire if they’re interested. Also, note that the platform offers insurance that can protect you if some of your client’s items are damaged or stolen while in your care.

In a recent development, how much can you make renting out extra space? It depends on how much space you have to rent and where it’s located. However, Neighbor.com indicates a range of rental space options that cost anywhere from $20 to $100+ per month.

Sources indicate that investing in dividend stocks is one of the best ways to earn money without a regular job. Many early retirees find a way to live and pay bills based solely on the dividends they receive from various stocks.

But what exactly is a dividend stock? For the most part, they are regular stocks but with a track record of sharing their profits with investors through dividends.

Dividends can also be earned in exchange-traded funds (ETFs) or mutual funds, and they can be significant once you build up a large portfolio.

Industry observers note that since dividends are paid by profitable companies, they tend to be seen as less risky for investors. If you’re curious about what it takes to get started with this strategy, this post explains how to invest in dividend stocks.

Housesitting is an option if you’re somewhat mobile and can move from place to place. Generally, you can find house-sitting gigs through word of mouth, referrals, or online portals like Craigslist.org or Facebook Marketplace.

That said, not all house-sitting gigs are paid. Some offer the potential for exotic travel instead and free lodging for a week to several months.

Either way, a website called TrustedHousesitters is the best place to find house-sitting gigs. Some jobs posted are for house-sitting only, while others require house sitters to provide basic care for pets or plants.

If you have serious wanderlust and want to travel far and wide, this platform can help make it happen. Many gigs posted online are in countries like Australia, Ireland, France, and Switzerland.

If you love animals and want to earn money taking care of them, several platforms can help turn your dream into a reality.

For example, Rover.com lets you provide basic care for dogs or cats in your home, or you can pick up dog walking gigs. Another mobile app, called Wag!, lets you do more of the same.

Recent findings suggest that you can set your rates for all types of work through these platforms, and your availability. While earnings vary by location and job, most people watch dogs and cats for anywhere from $40 to $100 per night.

It has been revealed that real estate investing may seem like a pipe dream if you hope to earn income without a job but hear me out. There are many ways to earn income through real estate without owning physical property or dealing with the hassles of being a landlord.

Industry observers note that you can invest in real estate investment trusts (REITs) that let you build wealth over time. You can also use a platform called Fundrise to invest in real estate with a minimum investment of $10.

Fundrise lets you purchase eREITs, large investment funds that acquire, own, or operate multi-residential and commercial properties. The income you earn is entirely passive since it handles the work of finding income-producing properties and managing them.

While returns are never guaranteed, Fundrise investors have achieved very solid returns. Investors who use the platform earned an average return of 7.31% in 2020, followed by 22.99% in 2021, 1.50% in 2022 and -7.45% in 2023 (their first down year).

It has been revealed that you can earn income on your spare change by investing it using Acorns. The roundup savings app syncs to your debit or credit card rounds up every purchase you make to the nearest dollar, and invests the difference. Once it’s set up, there’s no work on your part.

It has been revealed that most of the money is invested in ETFs and managed by the world’s top investment firms like Vanguard and BlackRock. While this app makes it easy to invest small amounts of money, it’s not free to use. Personal prepares start at $3 per month, while a family blueprint costs just $5.

If you’re looking for some paid gigs that are relatively easy, consider setting up a profile on TaskRabbit, an online platform that lets you get paid for completing various tasks, such as:.

Recent findings suggest that projects typically pay between $30 and $100, although some pay significantly more than that. TaskRabbit also lets you pick and choose the jobs you want to take on based on your availability so that you can work entirely on your schedule.

If you love taking photographs and have a knack for getting professional-looking images, you can use your skills and expertise to sell photos online.

Websites like Depositphotos and iStockPhoto pay photographers to supply them with stock photos they can sell to writers, publications, and various online platforms.

It has been revealed that the best part about this side hustle is that you can get started with the equipment you already have. While you can use a professional camera if you want to, many smartphones take professional-quality photos.

Earning a bank bonus is another way to earn money without a regular job, but you’ll need an upfront investment to get started. Most bonus offers require you to deposit a specific amount of money and keep it in your account for up to 12 months.

You may also be required to set up direct deposit to earn a bank bonus, and other terms and conditions may apply.

Where can you find the best bank bonuses? While bonus offers constantly change, you can start by checking with banks like Chase, HSBC, Radius Bank, and Wells Fargo.

Flipping furniture requires some upfront legwork and potentially even some artistic talent, but you can earn a solid income with this strategy if you know what you’re doing.

Essentially, this side hustle requires you to shop at thrift stores, garage sales, and online platforms to find furniture that will ultimately sell for more than you paid.

From there, you can sell the furniture as-is or clean it up and paint it with the goal of fetching an even higher price.

You can make money driving for Uber or Lyft on your own time, picking and choosing the days and hours you want to work.

Not only is rideshare work one of the most flexible side hustles, but you can earn $20 per hour and more with tips.

If you are low on free time but still want to make money without a job, consider selling stuff you don’t need. An array of online platforms makes it a breeze, although some platforms work better for selling.

For example, you can use Poshmark to earn money selling used clothing and accessories, while used electronics tend to sell best on platforms like eBay.com, Decluttr, BuyBackWorld, and Gazelle.

If you have home decor, furniture, or workout equipment to sell, you’ll almost always do better unloading those items locally on Facebook Marketplace.

Starting a YouTube channel is another way to earn money without a job, but that doesn’t mean it’s not work. The fact is, that creating quality videos and building an audience takes a lot of creativity and time. Plus, not everyone who tries to build a YouTube channel will succeed.

That stated, you can earn income without a regular job. I know because I have done it with my YouTube channel, Wealth Hacker.

How much you can earn on YouTube varies quite a bit, but it’s possible to earn thousands of dollars per month. If you’re curious about monetizing videos, my in-depth guide will show you how to make money on YouTube.

According to recent reports, donating plasma is a unique way to earn money without a job, although it’s not very glamorous. DonatingPlasma.org makes it easy to find plasma donation centers in your area, and you can earn as much as $100 for your first donation.

That said, subsequent plasma donations typically earn closer to $50. You’ll also be limited by the number of times you can donate plasma within a month. However, it’s possible to use this side gig to earn an extra $500 per month, which you can use to supplement your primary income.

Recent findings suggest that if you are willing to complete various tasks that help regular workers do their jobs, consider becoming a crowd worker. This gig will have you finishing up to-do lists of jobs that don’t require specific technical skills.

For example, you may get paid to proofread documents, label images, revision a resume, complete a form, or complete a data entry assignment.

Several platforms help you find crowd-working gigs, but the best ones include Microworkers and Clickworker.

If you want to do something simple that will get you moving, consider delivering groceries using apps like Instacart or Shipt. You get paid hourly, plus tips and all you have to do is head to the store, purchase groceries according to a list, and deliver them to people in your neighborhood.

The gig is extremely flexible, similar to driving for Uber or Lyft.

Another non-job gig lets you get paid to deliver packages for Amazon.com. You can do this through a platform called Amazon Flex, which promises its drivers anywhere from $18 to $25 per hour.

Unlike a regular Amazon job, Flex lets you pick the day and the hours you want to work. To get started, you need to create a free account, get approved, and start reserving blocks of time you want to deliver packages.

Sources indicate that finally, you can earn money by selling unwanted or unused gift cards in your possession. This hustle is made easy thanks to platforms like GiftDeals.com and CardCash.com.

It has been revealed that you won’t get the total value of your gift cards, but you should get 90% or more of the gift card balance for each card you sell. While selling gift cards for less than their total value may not seem ideal, it’s better than not using them and getting nothing in return.

Sources indicate that finally, you can earn small amounts of money by signing up with the best online survey sites. Not only is this side hustle as easy as it gets, but you can participate and get paid during your spare time and even on your phone.

Other online survey sites to check out include the following:.

Industry observers note that there you have it, 26 ways to make money without a job. While many of the jobs on our list won’t replace your 9-5, they can be a great way to increase your income so you can pay off debt or break the cycle of living paycheck to paycheck.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that open your donor-advised fund at Fidelity Charitable if you want one that takes any amount to start and private company shares at no extra charge. If you’re starting small, giving shares held at Schwab, or putting in $25,000 or more at once, pick the provider built for that.

Whichever provider you pick, the tax rules are the same. If you itemize rather than take the standard deduction, you count a gift toward your deductions in the year you put it in, then recommend grants to charities over time. Giving stock that has risen in value, held more than a year, usually beats selling it and donating the cash, since the capital gains tax on the rise never comes due. The grants can’t get you anything in return, either. An IRS notice treats a grant that pays for your tickets to a charity’s event as a benefit to you, which brings a penalty tax on whoever recommended it.

Sources indicate that we weighed each provider on what it takes to open an account and recommend a grant, its yearly fees and investment costs, the assets it takes, how fast grants go out, and who can take over the account. If you’re bunching several years of giving into one year so you can itemize, the fund holds that year’s gift while you spread the grants out.

It makes the best starting point for most givers, since it opens with any amount and charges nothing extra to take private tech giant shares and other assets that don’t trade publicly.

For more information, read our full Fidelity Charitable Review.

A giver starting small pays no administrative fee here, opens with $0, and can add or grant as little as $5 at a time.

For more information, read our full GoFundMe Giving Funds Review.

Schwab clients get the simplest way here to give shares held at Schwab, since the shares move online with no transfer form and the account has no minimum to open.

For more information, read our full DAFgiving360 Review.

Families can share one fund for $5 a month on contributions up to $50,000 a year, with as many as 24 members, and it takes more than 300 cryptocurrencies.

For more information, read our full Daffy Review.

Givers putting $25,000 or more in at once get pools built on Vanguard index funds and an administrative fee that drops to 0.11% on the part of a balance from $1 million to $5 million.

For more information, read our full Vanguard Charitable Review.

Fidelity Charitable fits most givers, and another provider here is worth choosing only when your gift’s size or the assets you hold match what it was built for. Move your gift in well before December 31 so the deduction counts this year.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A romantic date night at home feels like a night out when you plan it like one. Set a start time, pick a theme, put both phones in another room, and spend on one small treat instead of a restaurant bill. Take turns planning, so one of you always gets to be surprised.

In a recent development, dinner out costs what it does because you’re paying a restaurant to cook, serve, and clean up. The romance comes from the planning and the attention, and neither one costs anything at home.

Plenty of cheap evenings at home never feel like dates, because nobody planned them. So plan this one. Pick a start time and keep it the way you’d keep a reservation. Dim the lights, light candles, set the table with real plates, and put on music. Change out of what you wore all day, and leave both phones on silent in another room until the night is over.

Then choose one thing to spend on, such as a good steak, a better bottle of wine, or a bakery dessert, and keep everything else simple.

Say you go out once a month, and dinner for two with wine and dessert costs $120 with the tip. Cook a similar meal together at home, with a $15 bottle of wine as the treat and a homemade dessert by candlelight, and it costs about $35. You do the cooking and the dishes, and you keep $85 a month, or $1,020 a year.

Each of the 20 ideas below can be the night’s theme, and each comes with a rough cost for two. Parents can start any of them after the kids are asleep.

Shop a day ahead for these, so the evening starts with cooking instead of a grocery run.

A small bet, such as who does the dishes or picks the next movie, makes any of these more fun.

These suit a weeknight, when neither of you has the energy for a project.

These revisit your own history together, so most cost next to nothing.

Trade off who intends each date. The planner picks the idea and the treat and tells the other person only the start time and what to wear.

Pick the first idea today, put the start time on both calendars, and agree that whoever didn’t plan it plans the next one.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that lenders treat a duplex you live in as your home, so you can finance it with as little as 3.5% down on a government-insured FHA loan or 5% on a conventional loan.
  • In a recent development, buy the same duplex as a rental you won’t live in, and an FHA loan, which the Federal Housing Administration insures, is off the table.
  • FHA’s 3.5% minimum needs a credit score of 580 or higher, and scores from 500 to 579 need 10% down.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that lenders treat a duplex you live in as your home, so you can finance it with as little as 3.5% down on a government-insured FHA loan or 5% on a conventional loan. Buy one only if the other side’s rent, minus a quarter for repairs and empty months, leaves you paying less than a similar apartment rents for.

In a recent development, buy the same duplex as a rental you won’t live in, and an FHA loan, which the Federal Housing Administration insures, is off the table. A conventional loan, one without government insurance, then takes 25% down.

FHA’s 3.5% minimum needs a credit score of 580 or higher, and scores from 500 to 579 need 10% down. Freddie Mac, which buys many conventional loans from lenders, allows 5% down when its automated system approves the loan and the loan stays within a standard size limit, and 15% otherwise. Both loans require you to move in within 60 days and live there at least a year, after which you can move out and rent both sides.

Either way, the lender counts 75% of the rent the other side is expected to bring when it decides whether you can afford the payment. Fannie Mae, the other significant buyer, counts it only if you already pay rent or own a home.

Industry observers note that say you put $12,600, or 3.5%, down on a $360,000 duplex, and your full payment, with taxes and insurance that covers the rented side, is $3,000 a month. The other side rents for $1,900, and a similar apartment would rent for $2,000. The tenant’s rent leaves you $1,100 to pay. Set aside a quarter of that rent, $475, for repairs and months the unit sits empty, and your side costs $1,575, or $425 less than the $2,000 apartment. A gap like that makes the duplex worth buying if you’re ready to live next to your tenant.

You’ll likely share a yard with your tenant, screen applicants, and take repair calls yourself. A duplex also draws fewer buyers than a single-family home when you sell. If those trade-offs outweigh the savings, there are other ways to cut your housing cost by renting out part of your home, from a spare room to a basement unit.

Get two numbers before you bid: what similar units nearby rent for, from current listings, and your full monthly payment, from a lender’s quote.

To get that quote, compare the best mortgage lenders.

Tech Report: Federal Home Energy Tax Credits Ended – Check State & Utility Rebates Before You Sign

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (488 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Moneycrashers

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that the federal tax credits that covered up to 30% of the cost of insulation, heat pumps, windows, and home solar ended for work installed after 2025.
  • Industry observers note that the IRS ties the credits to the year the work was installed, not the year you paid, so a heat pump paid for in December 2025 and installed in January earns no credit.
  • Many utilities still pay rebates on heat pumps and insulation, and some states offer their own tax credits.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that the federal tax credits that covered up to 30% of the cost of insulation, heat pumps, windows, and home solar ended for work installed after 2025. Before you sign a contract, check what your utility and your state will pay, since many rebates pay only if you apply first or use an approved contractor.

Industry observers note that the IRS ties the credits to the year the work was installed, not the year you paid, so a heat pump paid for in December 2025 and installed in January earns no credit. Work installed by the end of 2025 still counts, and if your 2025 return left it out, you can claim it on an amended return with Form 5695 within three years of when you filed.

Many utilities still pay rebates on heat pumps and insulation, and some states offer their own tax credits. Some state energy offices also run one or both federally funded Home Energy Rebates programs. One pays up to $4,000 toward a whole-home upgrade at any income, and more to lower-income households. The other pays up to $14,000 for electric upgrades like heat pumps to households earning up to 150% of their area’s median income, though no longer to replace gas or oil equipment.

The federal credits came at tax time, after the job. A rebate program may need to approve your project and your contractor before the work begins, and it pays only for equipment that meets its efficiency rules.

Search your ZIP code on DSIRE, NC State University’s database of state and utility incentives, and on ENERGY STAR’s Rebate Finder. Then check your utility’s rebates page, and ask your state energy office whether its programs have opened. A home energy audit from your utility can also point you to rebates.

Recent findings suggest that redo the payback, the years an upgrade’s savings take to cover its cost, counting only rebates you’ve confirmed. Say your utility’s rebate is the same as in 2025, a heat pump would have earned the full $2,000 credit, and it cuts your bills by $500 a year. It now costs you $2,000 more than it would have in 2025, which adds four years to its payback. That extra cost can put the cheap upgrades that pay back fastest ahead of massive projects.

Before you sign, ask the contractor which of these programs it’s enrolled in, and get any approval a rebate requires in writing.

Sources indicate that having more than one type of debt is common, and that’s especially true once you graduate from college and start your first “real job.” You may have credit card debt, an auto loan, and a mortgage payment to make once you buy your first home. It’s also common to have other random debts to cover, including student loans.

Industry observers note that if you’re like many who took out loans during college, you will likely be paying them off after you graduate. In fact, 82% of students who borrowed loans expect to be making payments post-graduation, according to a recent College Ave Student Loans survey.

That remarked, you’ll want to make sure you’re balancing debt repayment with your savings goals along the way.

You’ll also want to make sure you’re paying down debts in the optimal order, or in a way that will help you save the most money on interest as possible while aligning with your goals. Which debts should you pay off first? Here’s a rundown of how to get the best results:.

No matter which types of debt you have, credit card debt should be your first priority. Why? Because credit card debt is likely the most expensive debt you have by far.

Federal Reserve data shows the average credit card interest rate on accounts assessed interest came in at around 22% as of May 2023, yet your credit card could easily be charging higher rates than the average.

To save as much money as possible, you should strive to pay as much as you can toward high-interest credit card bills each month. You can also pay down credit card debt faster with the help of a debt consolidation loan or a 0% APR balance transfer credit card.

Recent findings suggest that other unsecured debts like personal loan debt should come next in the debt payoff pecking order. After all, unsecured debts tend to have higher interest rates than secured debts like auto loans. In fact, the Federal Reserve also reported that the average interest rate on a 24-month personal loan came in at 11.48% as of May 2023, compared to the average rate of 7.81% on a 60-month auto loan.

Ideally, you’ll start paying more toward personal loan debt and other unsecured debts after all credit card debt is entirely paid off, although you should make at least the minimum payment on all your bills throughout the entire process.

The next debt you’ll want to tackle is your student loans. I suggest focusing on these loans after other unsecured debts, since federal student loans (and many private student loans) come with low fixed interest rates and monthly payments that will not change over time. If you have federal student loans, you may even want to look into income-driven repayment aims.

It has been revealed that if you’re hoping to pay down student loans faster or just want to save money on interest, you can also consider refinancing your student loans to get a shorter repayment timeline, a lower monthly payment, or both. Just remember that refinancing federal student loans can mean losing access to income-driven repayment plans and federal protections like deferment and forbearance.

Once you have paid off or substantially paid down all your other debts, you can focus your efforts on secured debts you have like mortgage loans and auto loans. These debts should be dealt with last since they are secured with collateral and tend to offer lower interest rates as a result. For example, you can consider paying more than the minimum on your mortgage, a car loan, or both until they’re paid off completely.

It has been revealed that then again, you may want to pay off debts with extremely low interest rates as slowly as possible to free up more cash flow for living expenses and investments. If you took out a mortgage in January of 2021 when the average interest rate on a 30-year, fixed rate home loan was as low as 2.65%, for example, it makes sense to make the minimum payment on that debt and invest your extra cash instead.

It’s vital to make sure you balance debt repayment with other financial considerations. After all, focusing too much on debt repayment early in life can leave you behind when it comes to investing for retirement or saving up for a first home.

While you’ll want to eliminate credit card debt and other high-interest debts as quickly as you can, even if you have to stop saving and investing for a while, you can pay down student loan debt and secured debts at a slower pace while saving and investing for the future along the way.

Industry observers note that finally, make sure you have adequate emergency savings throughout your entire debt payoff journey, or that you begin saving for emergencies as soon as you can. Without a fully funded emergency fund, you can end up relying on credit cards and other loans to get by and ruin your debt payoff progress in the process.

How much should you save? While most experts recommend having an emergency fund that can cover three to six months of expenses, it’s okay to start small if you have to.

Having more than one type of debt is how it works for most people, especially when you’re young and in the early stages of your career. When it comes to paying it off, however, you’ll want to make sure you have a concrete plan that can help you reduce interest charges and get where you want to be.

Focusing on credit card debt and other unsecured debts first always makes sense, since these debts aren’t secured by an asset and tend to charge much higher interest rates. You can focus on student loans next, followed by other secured debts you have like a home loan or car loan.

In a recent development, in the meantime, make sure you have an adequate emergency fund and invest in it for retirement. After all, debt won’t last forever if you’re serious about repayment, and saving and investing early can help you benefit from compound interest and avoid using credit cards for surprise expenses. Creating a budget to track these factors is your best bet.

If you need help creating one, or simply don’t know where to start, use this budget worksheet as your guide – you’ll reach financial freedom in no time.

Colorado Hiker Creates Ultimate Thru-Hike Across His Home State

📅 22 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1177 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Explorersweb

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Donovan Rice got into thru-hiking almost by accident.
  • According to recent reports, “I thought, there’s no way somebody can walk from Mexico to Canada.
  • From there, it was a slippery slope.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Donovan Rice got into thru-hiking almost by accident. Already outdoorsy, he graduated from long hikes to planning to climb all 53 of Colorado’s 14,000’ers (mountains above 14,000 feet, or 4,267m). While researching which peaks required overnight camping, he realized that some people’s hikes just keep going.

According to recent reports, “I thought, there’s no way somebody can walk from Mexico to Canada. That’s just ridiculous,” Rice explained. “I fell in love with that idea.”.

From there, it was a slippery slope. First came the Pacific Crest Trail (PCT), from the Mexican border in California to the Canadian border in British Columbia. Then he did the Continental Divide Trail (CDT), tracing the Rocky Mountains from Fresh Mexico to the Montana-Canada border. Before he knew it, he had a trail name — Iceman —and was working the gig economy to free up time for wilderness adventures.

But that’s where most people’s slippery slope levels out. Hiking the 4,988km CDT is as meaty a project as most of us can imagine. But for Rice, it only opened the floodgates. He was fascinated by everything that didn’t make it into famous routes, especially the ridges and mountains he passed in his home state of Colorado that were just off trail.

Sources indicate that “There’s all this stuff the CDT doesn’t hit because it is following the Continental Divide,” he told ExplorersWeb. “So when I got to the end of the Colorado section, about 700 miles, I was thinking, man, if there were a 2,000-mile version of that, it would be my dream thru-hike. Just that non-stop, relentless brutality that is Colorado.”.

Colorado has 14,000′ peaks but also deserts. Photo: Donovan Rice.

Industry observers note that rice started thinking about a massive thru-hike loop of the state. His idea was to stitch together existing trails and form upcoming ones where necessary.

In a recent development, “I dropped a load of pins across the areas in Colorado I wanted to visit, then I pulled out a public lands layer of the map to see how I might connect the areas,” he explained. “The three core design philosophies were beauty, breadth, and epicness. I wanted to see beautiful views, I wanted to cover as much of Colorado’s diversity as possible, and I wanted to take the most iconic and epic route possible.”.

Unlike places like the UK, there is no “right to roam” in Colorado, so connecting the route to avoid private land was tricky. Occasionally, he had to link bits of public land and sections of trail in the “least worst way,” with short road walks when private property appeared to halt progress.

As he tacked on mountain peaks and the national parks he wanted to explore, his route swelled to a monstrous 3,000km+. His itinerary now included all 11 of Colorado’s national forests, three of its national parks, 13 14,000’ers and 47 13,000’ers.

According to recent reports, “This is not an efficient route,” Rice admits. “You could walk the full perimeter of Colorado and then hike the Colorado Trail [an existing 885km trail from Waterton Canyon near Denver to Durango], and then still have kilometers left over [to complete the loop].”.

It has been revealed that the Great Colorado Route. Photo: Donovan Rice.

The route looked epic on paper, but Rice still needed to prove it could actually be thru-hiked. After months of planning, Rice set off on his Great Colorado Route from Gunnison National Park on May 14, 2026. He traveled ultra-light, carrying just six kilos of gear, with just a quilt instead of a sleeping bag and a tarp rather than a tent.

In a recent development, “I wanted it to be lightweight enough that I could be nimble on the mountains while doing these technical traverses,” stated Rice. Traveling light was wise. Rice’s Great Colorado Route is challenging, with plenty of scrambling and sustained time at altitude.

In a recent development, “The crux might be between Bailey and Rocky Mountain National Park. You go over the Mount Evans Wilderness, two 14,000’ers, hop on the Front Range across several 13,000’ers, and then across the Tenmile Range, and then the absolutely brutal Gore Range.”.

Sources indicate that rice spent 141 days tramping his trail, eventually finishing on October 1 after 3,252km. While he describes the route as “definitely not beginner-friendly” — due to plenty of cross-country terrain, off-trail navigation, and route-finding — it doesn’t require mountaineering skills.

Industry observers note that “For me, the real sweet spot is Class three scrambling,” he says. “Once you get up to Class four, it starts getting really scary, and I had no tolerance at all for true Class five rock climbing.”.

Recent findings suggest that however, he did pack an ice ax, micro-spikes, snow gaiters, and a lightweight helmet to protect against rockfall. He also made an effort to structure the route to provide relief between the most challenging sections, giving the trail an ebb and flow, and potential hikers time to decompress.

It has been revealed that the Ballard to La Junta traverse. Photo: Donovan Rice.

In a recent development, overall, his focus on scenic beauty over contrived difficulty helped keep the route somewhat accessible. This is notable because Rice hopes that other hikers will give it a go. He is building a website that maps the route, segment by segment, with GPS coordinates to help future hikers find the best places to camp or alternative paths depending on trail conditions. This is a May-through-October trail, but Rice stresses that it is unrealistic to expect perfect conditions for four and a half months.

In a recent development, “This is one of those routes where bailouts will have to happen,” Rice explained. “You’ll have to take a low route or an alternate. I’m hoping to revisit some of the areas in the future and establish some of these alternative routes.”.

He aims to get all 29 segments of the initial route fully mapped on The Great Colorado website by the end of the year. It’s a big project, almost as big as the hike itself.

According to recent reports, “I need to see how many people will actually give it a try. People can do segments. I’d love to see more thru-hikers do this, but the big challenge is that I think the majority of thru-hikers will look at this and think ‘that’s above my pay grade’.”.

The Castles, Colorado. Photo: Donovan Rice.

Once he finishes the website, the level of interest might dictate his next steps. “I don’t know what level of formal recognition I want to try for. Do I want to try to get it codified? Or should it stay unofficial and remain just some cool thing someone did that published information on how to do it yourself.”.

Whether or not his Great Colorado Route ever gains the name recognition of the CDT or PCT, Rice has authored something unique, and in a world full of rehashes and copycats, that makes it special.

Rice looking down on Island Lake from Ulysses S. Grant Peak. Photo: Donovan Rice.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that your 401(k) contribution limit starts over on January 1, and any room you don’t use by your last December paycheck is gone for good.
  • Recent findings suggest that doing this every January matters because the limit moves.
  • In a recent development, the limit counts contributions by calendar year, and every dollar has to come out of that year’s paychecks.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that your 401(k) contribution limit starts over on January 1, and any room you don’t use by your last December paycheck is gone for good. Each January, look up the new IRS limit, divide it by your number of paychecks, and set your contribution to that amount if your budget allows.

Recent findings suggest that doing this every January matters because the limit moves. The IRS adjusts it for inflation, and when it rises, a per-paycheck amount that maxed you out last year leaves room unused.

In a recent development, the limit counts contributions by calendar year, and every dollar has to come out of that year’s paychecks. It’s also a limit per person, not per job. If you switched employers this year, what went into the old plan counts too, and keeping the combined total under the limit is on you.

It has been revealed that to hit the max from any point in the year, take the current limit, subtract what you’ve already contributed, and divide by the paychecks you have left. Enter that as a dollar amount, or convert it to a percentage of your pay. If you’ll be 50 or older by December 31 and your blueprint offers catch-up contributions, you can add one on top, with a larger allowance in the years you turn 60 through 63. In a plan with a Roth option, the IRS requires the catch-up to go in as Roth, taxed now instead of at withdrawal, if your wages from that employer topped the high-earner threshold the year before.

Industry observers note that spread your contributions across the whole year if your employer matches each paycheck. Hit the limit by summer and the later paychecks can go unmatched, unless your initiative makes up the difference with a year-end true-up. Ask HR which kind you have.

If you changed jobs, add up both plans before you set the latest rate. Any excess has to come out by April 15 of the following year, or it’s taxed twice, once for the year you contributed it and again when you withdraw it.

Industry observers note that contribute at least enough to collect your whole employer match if the full limit is out of reach. Then put part of every pay raise toward a higher rate. Your take-home pay still grows, and contributions that rise faster than the limit shrink the gap to the max.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Farmland earns its owners a few percent a year in rent and has rarely lost value, but one farm deal can lock up your money for a decade. Start small by buying a farmland REIT, a firm that owns farms and trades like a stock, in your brokerage account or IRA.

Industry observers note that in 2008, as stocks crashed, the average value of U.S. farm real estate fell just 3.2%, its first drop since 1987, USDA reported. Its Land Values 2026 Summary shows only two dips since 2012, both about 0.3%.

Recent findings suggest that cash rent on U.S. cropland averaged $160 an acre in 2026, about 2.7% of the average acre’s $6,020 value, by the Economic Research Service’s figures. The rest of the return comes from the land’s price, which moves with crop prices and interest rates and can stall. Cropland gained 3.3% in 2026, but 0.3% after inflation.

Only two farmland real estate investment trusts trade publicly, Farmland Partners and Gladstone Land, and you can hold either in any brokerage account or IRA. Expect a bumpier ride than USDA’s numbers show, since the shares are priced every trading day while USDA’s land values come from a once-a-year survey of farm operators.

Platforms such as AcreTrader and FarmTogether sell stakes in single farms, but only to accredited investors. To qualify under SEC rules, you need a net worth over $1 million outside your home, or income over $200,000 ($300,000 for a couple) in each of the past two years and expected this year. Minimums are usually $15,000 or more, fees vary by deal, neither platform offers a resale market, and AcreTrader puts typical holds at five to 10 years. For most investors, a REIT is a better start than a platform deal.

Industry observers note that say you want 5% of a $500,000 portfolio, or $25,000, in farmland. In a single almond orchard deal, that money depends on one farm’s water supply and harvests for a decade. In a farmland REIT in your IRA, it’s spread across more than 140 farms, and you can sell any trading day.

Industry observers note that the SEC says REIT dividends are usually taxed at your regular income rate. Hold the REIT in an IRA, where they aren’t taxed as they’re paid, and keep farmland near 5% of your portfolio.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Too often, this talk happens after a fall or a stroke, when nobody can find anything.
  • It has been revealed that picture a daughter whose father is in intensive care.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Have the money conversation with your aging parents while everyone is healthy, not in a hospital hallway. You don’t need their net worth. You need to know where the documents are, who their advisors are, what insurance they carry, and whether a power of attorney exists.

Too often, this talk happens after a fall or a stroke, when nobody can find anything.

It has been revealed that picture a daughter whose father is in intensive care. His mortgage is due, his bank won’t discuss his accounts with her, and no one knows which company holds his life insurance. With no power of attorney on file, paying his bills may mean going to court.

Recent findings suggest that avoiding that can take one uncomfortable afternoon, and the list is shorter than you might fear. You aren’t asking what your parents are worth, the question that makes the talk feel like an audit. You’re asking what’s in place, where it is, and who handles it:.

Open with your own planning instead of theirs. Say you just named someone to make medical decisions for you and realized you don’t know what they’ve set up. A friend’s parent getting sick works, too. Let them decide how much to share and who takes each role.

Be ready for two hard truths. The money may be thinner than you assumed, so listen rather than judge. And trouble can show up first as money problems. The National Institute on Aging states money problems may be among the earliest signs of dementia, such as unpaid bills or a burst of new purchases, and scammers target older adults. People 60 and older reported more than $7.7 billion in fraud losses to the FBI in 2025.

Industry observers note that the money stays theirs, and so do the choices. Your part is making sure that if someone ever has to act for them, it’s the person they picked, doing what they asked.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This morning, rescuers found the bodies of Japanese climbers Hidesuke Taneishi, 40, and Tetsu Hashimoto, 25, on Gangapurna West.

“Both bodies were found at around 6,300m on the south side of Gangapurna West,” the rescue team told The Tourism Times.

Hidesuke Taneishi (left) and Tetsu Hashimoto (right) with a support team member in Kathmandu earlier this week. Photo: Cosmo Adventure.

The climbers were attempting the first ascent of the 7,140m mountain and lost contact on October 15 at approximately 7,050m on their summit push.

It has been revealed that A search-and-rescue team has been looking for the pair since October 19. Unfortunately, no one knew where they were on the mountain, or even if they were on the mountain at all. Therefore, the search started at Manang village, with no success.

The team included helicopter pilot Sobit Gauchan, high-altitude photographer and climber Manish Maharjan, and IFMGA mountain guide Pansang Rinzee Sherpa. The helicopter dropped Maharjan and Rinzee at 5,750m, and from there they used a drone to search the upper slopes. They scouted the northeast and southwest sides of the mountain, and finally found the remains of the Japanese climbers’ higher camp. Today, they found the bodies on the south side.

As for the cause of the accident, Rinzee told ExplorersWeb that their observations of the terrain pointed to a snow slab collapse.

Several teams have attempted Gangapurna West, located next to the Annapurna massif in Manang district, since it opened to foreign teams in 2014. However, none have summited. The mountain is also known as Asapurna or Lachenal Peak.

Team leader Hidesuke Taneishi was nominated for a Piolet d’Or last year after his first ascent of 6,652m Pholesobi Peak, also in Nepal, via a direct route up its vertiginous north face with Hiroki Yamamoto.

Hidesuke Taneishi on the summit of Pholesobi Peak. Photo: Hiroki Yamamoto.

#91454. How Unlimited Free Stuff from Amazon Almost Ruined My Retirement

📅 07 Oct 2025 • ⏱️ 10m • 📚 Deep Dive (2045 w)
